title: Mr S. & Kerry County Council
text:
Decision
Mr S. & Kerry County Council
From
Office of the Commissioner for Environmental Information (OCEI)
Case number: OCE-165129-N2J5R5
Published on 9 July 2026
Background
Scope of Review
Analysis and Findings
Decision
Appeal to the High Court
Whether the Council has carried out adequate searches pursuant to article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations.
9 July 2026
Background
1. On 24 June 2025 the appellant made an AIE request to Kerry County Council (the Council) which concerned the zoning status of a section of Cliffs in Ballybunion. On 14 July 2025 the Council sought to invoke article 9(2)(a) of the AIE Regulations, contending that the request was manifestly unreasonable and seeking engagement from the appellant to refine its scope.
2. On 14 July 2025, the appellant refined the scope of his request to:
“1. All records relating to the rezoning decision
Including:
• The planning report(s) and internal briefing documents that informed or supported the rezoning decision.
• Minutes or summaries of internal meetings (including senior planning staff or management) where the rezoning was discussed.
• Any communications between Fáilte Ireland and the Council regarding the rezoning.
2. All records demonstrating legal and environmental compliance
Including:
• Any related legal or planning advice.
• Any screening reports or assessments undertaken for Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) or Appropriate Assessment (AA) specifically in relation to this rezoning.
Any correspondence or submissions received from the NPWS or other statutory bodies during the plan-making process, specifically referencing this area or the potential impact on the SAC
Do you have a link to any pre-draft submissions or other preliminary public or stakeholder consultations?”.
3. On 19 August 2025 the Council invoked article 7(2)(b) to extend the deadline by which the decision was due to the respondent, by one month.
4. On 13 October 2025 the Council issued its original decision which stated that it was granting the request, it simultaneously relied upon article 7(5) however to refuse access to some elements of the information sought on the basis that it did not hold it; therefore, it is more accurate to state the request was partially granted.
5. The original decision states:
“The planning department have confirmed the Councils website contains all records as part of the Statutory process. The first link previously supplied would have contained the draft records and Material Alterations.
The planning department has identified no records which deal specifically with the change in zoning. The below link to Kerry County Councils website provides the
• Local Area Plan
• SEA Statement
• Natura Impact report
Listowel Municipal District Plan 2020-2026 | kerrycoco.ie
• Minutes of Listowel Municipal District Meeting September 2020 lap20.pdf
Pre-draft consultation was carried out in 2018 (8th Feb 2018 to 23rd March 2018) and the Council received 11 submissions. The planning department have reviewed the submissions. There was no specific submission in relation to Ballybunion settlement. There was no submission from the NPWS or Failte Ireland.
1 Schedule of records
The planning department has reviewed the file in relation to the Listowel Municipal District Local Area Plan 2020-2026. The following records have been identified:
1 LMD SEA Scoping Report issued in April 2018 prior to the plan being prepared.
2 Listowel Scoping Submissions received
3 Version of Ballybunion Maps
o May 2018
o November 2018
o December 2018
o September 2019
o October 2019
o September 2020
The planning department has confirmed the May 2018 map would be the first version prepared when work started on the Draft Local Area Plan. Subsequent versions would include changes to the draft. The planning department has not identified any record outlining the changes between versions.
2 Findings, particulars and reasons for decision to deny access
The sections of the AIE Regulations which can apply to deny access to documents are known as its exemption provisions.
Section 7 of the Regulations sets out
(5) Where a request is made to a public authority and the information requested is not held by or for the authority concerned, that authority shall inform the applicant as soon as possible that the information is not held by or for it.
The Planning department has not identified specific records in relation to the change of zoning of the area identified on the maps provided”.
6. On 16 October 2025 the appellant requested an internal review decision.
7. On 18 November 2025 the Council issued its internal review decision, affirming the original decision.
8. The appellant appealed to this Office on 30 November 2025.
9. I have been directed by the Commissioner to undertake a review under article 12(5) of the Regulations. In carrying out my review, I have had regard to the submissions made by the appellant and the Council. In addition, I have had regard to:
a. the Guidance document provided by the Minister for the Environment, Community and Local Government on the implementation of the AIE Regulations (the Minister’s Guidance);
b. Directive 2003/4/EC (the AIE Directive), upon which the AIE Regulations are based;
c. the 1998 United Nations Economic Commission for Europe Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-Making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters (the Aarhus Convention); and
d. The Aarhus Convention—An Implementation Guide (Second edition, June 2014) (‘the Aarhus Guide’).
Scope of Review
10. In accordance with article 12(5) of the AIE Regulations, my role is to review the public authority's internal review decision and to affirm, annul or vary it.
11. My review in this case is concerned with whether the Council has carried out adequate searches pursuant to article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations.
Analysis and Findings
7(5)
12. Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations is the relevant provision to consider, where the question arises as to whether the requested environmental information or any further environmental information is held by, or for, the public authority concerned. It provides as follows:
“Where a request is made to a public authority and the information requested is not held by or for the authority concerned, that authority shall inform the applicant as soon as possible that the information is not held by or for it.”
13. What will be considered reasonable will vary from case to case, but as a general guide, I set out below the type of information that my Office would generally expect to be set out in a decision where a public authority is relying on article 7(5) of the Regulations:
i. an outline of exactly which areas/units etc. of the organisation were searched for the information.
ii. an explanation of how searches were carried out (i.e. manually, by computer, by name, by key words).
iii. Keywords should be recorded and provided in the decision as appropriate. details of the individuals consulted in connection with the search.
iv. a description of the searches carried out to cover the possibility of misfiled/misplaced records.
v. details of guidelines, practices, procedures and arrangements in relation to the storage, filing, archiving, retention and destruction of the type of information requested in this case.
14. In this case the appellant is not satisfied that the Council have conducted adequate searches pertaining to all information falling within the scope of the request, with particular emphasis on the Council’s statement that it does not hold any records in relation to any change in the zoning status of the area to which the request concerns. The appellant notes that the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) report with respect to the area in question, released as part of the AIE request, identifies the “environmental factors to be considered for the Local Area Plan” however that it “does not demonstrate that environmental legislation was applied or that the rezoning decision was informed by the SEA process”.
15. The appellant further describes the Council’s submission that the land rezoning may have resulted from changes in Tailte Éireann background mapping, as “not credible”
, contending that “…a cartographic update cannot justify altering zoning within a Natura 2000 site. Even if the cliffs appeared differently on the updated map, any resulting change to zoning layers would have required internal instructions, discussions, and environmental checks. The assertion that no such records exist is inconsistent with normal planning processes”.
16. In its submission to this Office, the Council contend that it has undertaken satisfactory searches to identify records pertaining to the information sought. With respect to the land in question, it states:
“The Planning Dept. has reviewed its files and does not have any additional records that it can provide. All relevant material relating to the adoption of the Listowel Municipal District Local Area Plan 2020-2026 has been provided. There are no other records in relation to the zoning of individual plots of land or amendments to zonings/settlement boundaries prior to the publication of the Draft LAP which was published on October 31st, 2019. The box file/hard copies in relation to this Local Area Plan are available for inspection in the Planning Dept. Our digital files have also been reviewed and apart from different versions of zoning maps, which have been provided, there are no records/documents in relation to changes made from one version to the next”.
Detailing associated searches, it notes:
“All relevant folders which contain plans have been searched. All documentation containing the records are held on the hard drive under M:\Planning_New\PPolicy\Forward_Planning\Municipal District Plans\4.Listowel There would be no mobile phone messages and emails (the plan was prepared in 2019). We have searched emails for “cliff” and no relevant results for Ballybunion”.
17. With respect to the appellant’s request for records relating to submissions on the draft consultation and legal and environmental compliance, it states:
“Kerry County Council did not receive submissions from Fáílte Ireland in relation to the Listowel MD LAP. A submission from Fáilte Ireland was therefore not received on the Draft LAP or in relation to pre-draft consultation which took place early 2018. We provided copies of the various Environmental Assessments, SEA Scoping report and versions of Ballybunion Maps.
The NPWS did not make a submission on the Draft LAP. SEA Scoping took place in April/May 2018. The NPWS also did not make a submission on the SEA Scoping. Kerry County Council provided copies of the various Environmental Assessments, SEA Scoping report and versions of Ballybunion Maps.
Website links provided to Mr S. contained all records as part of the Statutory process; this would have included the draft records and material alterations. The planning department has identified no records which deal specifically with the change in zoning.
Links were also provided which detailed:
• Local Area Plan
• SEA Statement
• Natura Impact report
• Minutes of Listowel Municipal District Meeting September 2020”.
18. In reviewing the appellant’s submission with respect to his appeal, I note his contentions with respect to the legal context of re-zoning land, to include obligations on public bodies pursuant to the Habitats Directive, SEA Directive, and Planning and Development Act 2000. I also acknowledge information he has provided regarding historical FOI requests to the Council for information relevant to this appeal and his position with respect to the connection between the land in question and other Council records to include the Ballybunion draft Development Plan July 2020 and the Kerry County Tourism Strategy and Action Plan 2026-2022
.
19. It is my view that in this case the appellant’s contentions that further information and records exist, arises in the context of an expectation of information a public authority would be expected to have if it undertook an exercise to re-zone land, according to legal and environmental obligations. These contentions are outlined further by the appellant in the context of his previous FOI requests which yielded other records he suggests are relevant and, adjacent Council documents which concern the townland and area (to include the zoned land in question).
20. In considering the above, I have also reviewed the submission from the Council which is consistent with its reasoning at original and internal review stage that no further records are held with respect to the zoned land in question, either by or for it. It is the Council’s position that no re-zoning has taken place, attributing the variation in maps to “mapping changes”,
further stating in its internal review decision that “Kerry County Council use Tailte Éireann as background maps to which to place zoning maps over. There was a significant change in the style of maps used between the Tailte Éireann background map used in 2020 and the map used in 2013. Tailte Éireann show the cliffs as ‘Sand, sand and shingle” and “embankment”.
21. In reviewing the Council’s search details concerning the information being sought, outlined at paragraph 16 and 17 I am persuaded that adequate searches have been undertaken such to reasonably conclude that further information is not held by or for it. This belief stems from my consideration of the nature of the information itself, the locations searched/search terms used and, the relevance of the Council’s view that no re-zoning has taken place, but rather that the difference may be attributed to historical mapping data. Notwithstanding my view that the search information provided has met the threshold of 7(5) in this case, I find it logical to assume that if the Council are of the view that the land was not re-zoned, then information and records associated with a re-zoning process are not held by or for it.
22. While it is the appellant’s view that this information should exist, it is outside the remit of this Office to adjudicate on how public authorities carry out their functions generally, including with respect to their environmental information management practices. I have no role in assessing how public authorities collect, maintain and disseminate environmental information. My role concerns reviewing appeals of requests for access to environmental information within the scope of the request, which is held by or for the relevant public authority and no more than that.
23. Indeed, if this land has in fact been rezoned then the appellant is correct to assert and expect specific legal and environmental activities and therefore records, to exist, however the question of whether this has taken place, and accordingly whether it ought to have taken place, is outside of the remit of this Office.
24. The information the Council have provided at internal decision stage and within its submission to this Office with respect to searches undertaken, combined with its position that the information does not exist as it was not legally necessary to produce, leads me to reasonably conclude that it has met its obligations under article 7(5).
Decision
25. Having carried out a review under article 12(5) of the AIE Regulations, I affirm the Council’s decision.
Appeal to the High Court
26. A party to the appeal or any other person affected by this decision may appeal to the High Court on a point of law from the decision. Such an appeal must be initiated not later than two months after notice of the decision was given to the person bringing the appeal.
Gemma Farrell
Senior Investigator
Office of the Commissioner for Environmental Information
